Vampire Survivors has spawned a tidal wave of copycats. Some of them add a twist that helps them stand out in the crowd, some of them do nothing interesting and bank on their genre to pull players in. Sodaman is the latter. The meta-progression is boring and incredibly overpowered (I only ever died once or twice across several dozen matches). The abilities are boring and lack interesting combos. The game isn't built to handle what it throws at you (endgame on an rtx 3080 will get you as low as 10fps depending on your build). The bosses are INSANELY easy and offer 0 threat whatsoever. Once you have meta items, you can literally kill them in 0.001s of their intro ending. I'll keep an eye on its development, but this is one of the least interesting survivors games on the market.

Most similar games include other objectives/interactables to be less tedious. - Skill points are bought with the same currency that is used for guns and cyberware, which is excessive. The game is not much in it's current state, but to be fair it is in early access and really cheap. I'll probably come back to this when it fully releases.

At first the game feels like it is going with some kind of Cyberpunk Defenders of the Galaxy with Soda vibe. Works for a roguelite premise. Also I am a sucker for pixelated games. The issue with the game is that it leans on that without putting polish into much and leaving an AI to write and voice the dialogue within the game. Dialogue that the game that they are very invested in having you stop everything you are doing to go and interact with. "What are you doing?" "What am I doing?" "What is this this a menu?" "Huh?" "Sorry, I was just breaking the tension." So it's a game in of itself to try and click past whatever they are on about so you can get back to playing the game. It isn't even like they are poking fun at the stilted dialogue or anything either. Not in any entertaining way at least... The gameplay feels serviceable at first and similar to Death Must Die with more shooting, but the game has a host of issues from going to black screen when you adjust the audio bars more than it would like to the sound going crushy and awful after a few runs. Hit checks are moderately bad. Sometimes you are struck by a projectile or damage area once. Sometimes it is anywhere from 2 to 5 times or more. It all depends on how you are moving. Sometimes standing still literally is the best option for some hit areas because you are more likely to be hit ONCE. One run a single projectile from a boss created a cloud of damaged numbers that inflicted over a hundred damage in the blink of the eye. I could only tell because the game does a dramatic scene when your character 'perishes' so I could clearly see that I was hit for 7 nearly twenty times. I guess it is a game of 'don't get hit' then. Oh and there are a host of typos and other issues like skills giving the wrong effects or telling you that they give you incorrect effects. Soda Damage up 6%, but also it has a flip to it telling you that about what toxic does. Weird. Either way, this Sodaman needs a bit more work. More fizz in the can, more love in every sip? I don't know. It feels like there was some effort at first and then it was limp wristed at the end. It could have been a nice cheap quick game to set down and pick up on occasion, but it isn't.

After I have a few abilities in use, the game will just drop frames as it triggers all the effects on a wave of enemies. This isn't Path Of Exile. I shouldn't go from 110 fps to 20 every time I nuke a wave from orbit. Aside from the horrendous programming, the game itself is alright. 5.5/10 for the fundamentals, but 3/10 for execution. Stay away.

One of my favorite early-access games on steam that got fully finished yesterday. Good take on the survivorslike/bullet-heaven genre,with a Duke Nukem-esque protagonist who likes fizzy drinks. The game has a lot of upgrades which you can mishmash to suit your playstyle,and you have a rather large permanent skill tree you unlock with currency. There are also cybernetic enhancements which are pretty decent (I prefer the crit chance+ricochet+damage+exp equipment,even if the EXP boxers were nerfed from 150 EXP to 20 and thus you can no longer get all soda upgrades in a run). Music and pixel artstyle are well-made aswell,I just wish we had an option to make our runs shorter or longer in Chaos mode,so we could have higher levels and get more OP (and faster) over time,and that there was an epilogue after beating the final boss,and be able to play the third planet's chaos mode from there. Overall score : 9.5/10

The absurd throwaway story with AI voiceover is a potential one, but the technical issues are the real show stopper. I've only played for about 80 minutes and had a crash to desktop, a full OS lockup, two other game freezes and there is a pervasive audio bug where you essentially have to turn the sound off or the sound effects will eventually devolve into static. Has potential especially on sale, but it needs some definite bug squashing time put in. As is it's a hard sell in any world where Vampire Survivors, Yet Another Zombie Survivors, Deep Rock Survivor and Nimrods exist.

I picked up Sodaman for the price of a few sodas, and somehow it delivered more entertainment than the actual sodas. The game wastes absolutely no time. Within minutes you’re already blasting through enemies like you accidentally drank a 12-pack of energy drinks mixed with liquid confidence. The progression is fast, the action is nonstop, and before long you’re so overpowered that the enemies should probably be filing complaints with HR. I usually hate games that take 10 hours to “get good.” Sodaman basically walks up and says, “Nah, here’s a ridiculous weapon, go cause problems.” And honestly? I respect that. For the cost of a couple drinks from a gas station, you get a surprisingly addictive game that lets you become an unstoppable, caffeine-fueled force of destruction almost immediately.

Adding to the negative review pile, buyers beware! AI usage! The bloody nerve to not disclose AI use until *after* the 1.0 release, *after* being featured in a humble bundle? Truth be told, I don't buy the claim AI was limited to just concept art and voice acting - the game runs and plays like a hot mess, and you can find reddit posts from a few years ago where the devs were asking about AI usage for language translations. Sure would explain the bizarre writing... and if it isn't AI? Welp, you still have a slightly less dirty turd. AI aside, this game fails at being an engaging roguelike. Runs and objectives feel like slogs (which other roguelikes with similar run lengths manage to avoid), balancing feels as if it was decided by throwing darts at a board, and the galore of technical issues you can read up here should say plenty. Seriously, want a good game of this kind? If you don't have Vampire Survivors already, I'd recommend Army of Ruin, a really great clone of that game. As for this game, however? Shady devs, flimsy game, tiring 100%, AI weirdness... just stay away from this one.

Soda Man is a relatively well-executed isometric bullet heaven featuring gorgeous pixel art and animation. Its aesthetic is an entertaining collision of modern cyberpunk, Duke Nukem-style irreverence, anime, and dark sci-fi fantasy—all blended together into one gloriously chaotic package with a lighthearted sense of humor. The Soda theme is interesting and reminded me of Mullet MadJack, the weapons and accessibility options are well-executed, the supporting cast are unimpressive cardboard archetypes, and the upgrades are ridiculous in the most awesome ways possible. Where the game stumbles is its voice acting. It appears to have been generated by a fairly mediocre AI, and, more importantly, it feels as though the developers never performed even the most basic quality checks. The AI attempts to literally pronounce written laughter ("hehehehe") and even reads aloud placeholder censorship symbols for profanity, resulting in lines like "number, percent, dollar, exclamation" instead of simply treating "#%$!" as a censored curse. These moments are so frequent and jarringly unnatural that they repeatedly pull you out of the experience. Ironically, the written dialogue itself isn't nearly as bad; it's the AI narration that undermines it. It's a disappointing blemish on an otherwise enjoyable and visually striking bullet heaven.

played this for way too long before I learned about all the AI slop in the game and the devs' choice to obscure that fact until after a full release. There's not much to say that hasn't already been said in other reviews but to hit the main points: - The AI voice work is garbage, there's no reason to avoid paying some randos on fiverr to do a better job - Gameplay feels lacking in just about every department; the upgrade/build system seems good until you put in over a dozen runs and figure out that you can't make a cohesive build, just overpowered randomness. - No cohesion between map size and boss fights. The game wants you to constantly run around for upgrades, which isn't a bad idea, but then it locks you into a tiny arena for boss fights, so if the boss is too hard you can't even go grab the upgrade chest that is just out of reach of the arena. Granted, it's rare that a boss is too hard, but there are a couple that are absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and they really demonstrate the weakness of the arena idea. - Meta progression is stupid, to go along with the AI voice complaint why on earth did you need all this "story" and all these "characters" in a game that's basically just Vampire Survivors? The choice to include a populated hub and then fill it with clankers is baffling, none of it was necessary in terms of providing the player with a sense of meta progression, just have Sodaman go back to his spaceship and upgrade his own stuff in silence. - Even if you skip through all of the dialogue like i did, it's still painfully apparent that everyone around Sodaman exists either to suck his ♥♥♥♥ (both literally and figuratively) or to be turned into a pile of red goo. It's not that a game like this can't work with a story and characters, it's that this specific game had no business trying to have either. TL;DR AI slop game, avoid this studio -
